text:
Dear Partners,

There's an old saying where I grew up: when the creek rises fast, it's not always the deepest part of the river doing the work — sometimes it's just runoff finding the path of least resistance. That's a fair way to describe the quarter's public markets. Public equities rallied +9.0%, credit spreads tightened to 380bps over, and the central bank held its policy rate at 4.75% while inflation sat at 2.7%. A lot of that move looks like exuberance finding a channel, not necessarily a durable widening of the river itself.

We say this because we know you'll ask about the gap. Our reported return this quarter was +0.5%, against +1.0% year-to-date and +28.0% since inception — figures we stand behind, not figures we're proud to explain away. Listed comparables rerated sharply this quarter, and the public rally has, in the newsflow's own words, left private marks behind. We don't chase that. Our NAV index sits at 101.0, a deliberate, unhurried mark that reflects underlying cash flows and covenant packages, not a ticker refreshing every seventeen seconds. Public markets vote daily; we prefer to let the fundamentals speak, quarter by quarter, the way a good tenant farmer reports the harvest rather than the weather.

On the portfolio itself, our conversations with borrowers continue in the spirit we described last quarter — constructive amendments where covenants have needed adjusting, worked out in partnership rather than confrontation. We remain lenders first, partners always, and structural seniority continues to anchor our recovery expectations across the book. Where terms are being reset, they are being reset with our capital's protection in mind, not merely the borrower's convenience.

Looking ahead, we would be doing you a disservice if we pretended the rerating in public comps carries no signal at all. Should that repricing persist, or should credit conditions tighten further than the current 380bps would suggest, we may see additional amendment activity across the portfolio — and we think that's a prudent thing to watch rather than fear. Structural seniority has not yet been tested by a full cycle at our current scale, and we say that plainly, not to alarm you, but because a partnership built on straight talk works better than one built on comfortable silence.

We believe recovery is likely to remain the base case across the vast majority of our positions. But "likely" is a word we use with care, not with certainty, and we'd rather earn your trust one honest quarter at a time than borrow it against a rally we didn't build.

As always, our door — and our covenants — remain open to your questions.

With appreciation and candor,
Stonebeck Credit
